content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents to identify all relevant project documents, especially candidate_specs.md and any documents containing simulation rate-vs-threshold, signal efficiency, allocated trigger rate, and Level-1 FPGA latency results."},{"id":"s2","description":"Read candidate_specs.md. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, assign them stable numeric IDs 1, 2, and 3 for tracking, and note any documented constraints or parameters for each candidate."},{"id":"s3","description":"Read the simulation/performance documents identified in s1. For each candidate algorithm and each available threshold between 20 and 60 GeV, extract the signal efficiency and trigger rate; also extract the allocated trigger rate. Record the allocated trigger rate and the numeric efficiency/rate values needed for comparison."},{"id":"s4","description":"Read the Level-1 FPGA latency documentation. For each candidate algorithm, extract the hardware latency in microseconds and determine whether it satisfies the hard 4.0 us maximum. Record each candidate's latency numerically."},{"id":"s5","description":"Filter all candidate-threshold options to those using one of the three listed candidates, threshold between 20 and 60 GeV, latency <= 4.0 us, trigger rate <= allocated rate, and signal efficiency >= 80%. Among the surviving options, identify the one with the highest signal efficiency; if there is a tie, choose the option with the lowest trigger rate, then the lowest latency."},{"id":"s6","description":"Record the selected candidate numeric ID, selected threshold in GeV, expected signal efficiency, expected trigger rate, allocated trigger rate, and FPGA latency. Also record a numeric pass/fail flag for each hard requirement so the reporting module can prepare the final recommendation."}]}
